Subject: Renewal pricing discussion — flexible uplift & co-term request

Hi Priyom,

Hope you’re doing well — we’re starting renewal planning for NeuroLytics and want to discuss pricing for an expected mid-contract growth. Quick context: we’re currently on a committed plan with Redwood (200M tokens/month committed, co-term March 2027). Our Q4 product roadmap has a new inference feature that could push monthly usage to ~350M tokens/month for 3–5 months starting November.

Key asks:
- Can Redwood provide a path to short-term uplift (Nov–Mar) that preserves a co-term with our current March 2027 renewal?
- What discount or blended-rate options are available for an incremental committed uplift vs a temporary top-up (one-off credits)?
- Any billing/PO implications if we need signoff within two weeks?

Attached a usage export and our projected token sheet for November–March. Happy to jump on a 30-min call, but if you can send options via email that would help our procurement review.

Thanks,
Olivia Chen
Head of ML Platform
NeuroLytics

Hi Olivia — thanks for the context and the attachments, very helpful. I pulled the usage report and chatted with our pricing ops — below are three pragmatic paths we commonly offer for this pattern. I’ll outline tradeoffs so you can route to procurement quickly.

Option 1 — Staged Top-up (short-term, minimal contract change)
- Add a time-bound top-up credit pool that covers expected overage (e.g., 150M tokens/month for Nov–Mar).
- No change to co-term; existing March 2027 renewal remains.
- Pricing: pay-as-you-go on top-up at list rate with a volume rebate of 5% applied to the uplift if paid upfront.
- Billing: single invoice for top-up; PO ok for one-time credit purchase.

Option 2 — Temporary Commit Uplift + Co-term (recommended if growth sustains)
- Amend current commit to increase committed tokens for Nov–Mar and then revert to baseline or negotiate next term.
- Pricing: blended uplift rate (example: 6% discount on uplift tiers for the committed months).
- Requires a simple amendment and sign by procurement; co-term preserved.

Option 3 — Annualize now + Blended Discount (best for long-term predictability)
- Annualize the uplift into a higher committed band through March 2027 (effectively grab extra committed volume now).
- Pricing: deeper blended discount (8–10%) depending on the size of the annualized uplift and prepayment.
- Involves contract amendment and finance approval for invoicing change.

Additional: We can layer a "surge guard" buffer (10% burst capacity) for any short peaks to avoid throttling, billed separately at a nominal fee.

Next steps I propose:
1) Tell me which option you'd like to pursue (1/2/3) and confirm target peak month usage.
2) If Option 2 or 3, I’ll loop in Marissa for commercial approval and Ben for finance & invoicing cadence.

I attached a draft of the terms we’d use for a staged top-up for your procurement team to preview.

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_Flex-Topup-Terms_v1.docx]

Marissa / Ben — forwarding NeuroLytics request. TL;DR: potential Nov–Mar uplift to ~350M tokens/mo (baseline 200M). Olivia asked for co-term-preserving options; I proposed three: staged top-up, temporary commit uplift, or annualize early.

My read: NeuroLytics is likely to prefer minimal contract friction but wants some discount on committed uplift. I think we can be competitive at 6% on a temporary commit uplift (Option 2) if we include a 10% surge guard and standard prepay for the uplift months. That keeps margins reasonable and keeps procurement happy.

Ben — can you confirm the margin impact on a 6% uplift discount for a 5-month elevated window (Nov–Mar) with a prepay? Also flag any billing/PO constraints if they sign with a one-time amendment rather than annualizing.

Marissa — if you’re comfortable, can we offer a one-time exec-facilitated 6% uplift discount and include a DocuSign path for quick signature? If not, suggest a counter (I’m thinking 5% with a 1-month notice requirement).

Thanks,
Priyom

Priyom / Marissa — ran a quick margin calc on Option 2 (temporary commit uplift at 6% discount for Nov–Mar). Assuming uplift volume of ~750M tokens/month net across the uplift band (combined uplift months), the uplift revenue at list would be ~$36k/month; at 6% discount that's ~$33.8k/month — gross margin impact is moderate but acceptable given the higher renewal probability and reduced churn risk.

A couple of practical notes:
- If they prepay the uplift months, we should recognize revenue per our current policy but finance will need PO referencing the amendment.
- If procurement insists on a single PO that covers both uplift and baseline, the contract language needs to be explicit about the time-bound nature of the uplift.
- Approve a DocuSign quick path for amendments; legal prefers a short SOW amendment template which I've reviewed and can sign off on.

Approve: 6% uplift discount + 10% surge guard, conditional on prepay for the uplift months. I’ll prepare the finance memo and the revenue/recognition blurb for legal.

Ben Carter
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference
